newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast refined prods eases with API report.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast refined prods eases with API report.

text.p: Wholesale prices for U.S. West Coast refined products eased Tuesday, pressured by growing inventories, traders said.
West Coast unleaded gasoline inventories rose 520,000 barrels last week, according to the American Petroleum Institute (API), putting pressure on prices to fall further, traders said late Tuesday.
The West Coast build offset slightly lower production levels of 1.4 million barrels, and a drop in refinery use, traders said.
Refinery utilization fell 1.4 percentage points last week to 96.9 percent, leaving traders hopeful that refiners' lower appetite for expensive crude oil would improve downstream profits.
Traders said the exceptionally low product prices began to revive buying Tuesday, with refiners opting to buy supply rather than make it.
"I think refineries are contemplating deep run cuts," one refinery trader said.

June supplies of Los Angeles cleaner-burning CARB consel was bid and offered two cents lower Tueday at 55.50/56.50 cents, while conventional gasoline and reformulated sold at one cent lower, dealers said.
A West Coast refiner sold 100,000 barrels in San Francisco for 56 cents a gallon, but the buyer was not immediately available to confirm the deal.
